title: Sam Morgan's advice, Chris Kelly, and Joyce McCullen's orchestra
summary: Sam Morgan encouraged him and he took over from a drummer to play with Chris Kelly at the Bulls Club for about three years, then with McCullen's orchestra.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: So, Morgan, Sam Morgan's come by every night. He said, boy you're going to be a good drummer someday. He said, now you should show me how to put that left foot and right foot down and keep the time with the music. So after a while, Morgan needed a drummer. Well he'd take me to the boy, just like I tell you, the boy Roy was playing with Sam Morgan. That told me to go with Chris Kelly. You heard talk of him? Oh yeah. I worked with Chris Kelly for many years at the Bulls Club. That's where we started, the Bulls Club. Well I played with Chris Kelly for about three years. I had first just got married, just after I got married in 1925. And we played in different places, all out of town. And after I played with Chris Kelly, I quit Chris, went with Joyce McCoy, went with Joyce McCullen. I heard talk of him.
You had a brass band too, didn't you?
